goldens.comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:142 — The working-hours end check reuses the slot start, so a booking that starts before closing but ends after it is accepted.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at lines 138-145 in the diff, the code calculates both `start` and `end` using the same formula: `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`. This means `end` equals `start`, so the check `end > workingHour.endTime` will never properly validate if a booking that starts before closing time but ends after it. The `end` variable should use `slotEndTime` instead of `slotStartTime` to properly check if the slot extends beyond working hours.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:139 — Using `find` treats any other same-day working-hours interval as a rejection, so schedules with split shifts reject slots that fit one interval.

adjudication.rationale: The code at lines 131-145 uses `find` to check if a slot is outside working hours. The logic returns `true` (marking slot as outside working hours) if `start < workingHour.startTime || end > workingHour.endTime` for ANY matching day. With split shifts (e.g., 9-12 and 14-17), a slot at 10:00 would be rejected because it's outside the 14-17 interval, even though it fits the 9-12 interval. The `find` returns on the first match that fails the condition, rather than checking if the slot fits ANY of the working hour intervals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — The date-override equality check compares two newly created Dayjs objects by reference, so equal start/end sentinel overrides are never detected.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 114 in the diff (within the checkIfIsAvailable function), the code `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes'))` compares two Dayjs objects using `===`. In JavaScript, this compares object references, not values. Two separately created Dayjs objects representing the same moment will never be `===` equal because they are different object instances. This should use `.isSame()` method instead. This is a real bug that would cause the sentinel override detection to never work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:114 — No test exercises a zero-length date override, leaving the new closed-day availability path unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new logic at line 114 that handles zero-length date overrides (when start === end, representing a closed day). Looking at the condition `if (dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes') === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, 'minutes'))`, this is a specific code path for closed days. The test file only adds a test for timezone handling with date overrides that have actual time slots, not a zero-length override scenario. The finding correctly identifies that this specific new code path lacks test coverage.
